title: A drawing under the pointer
description: How one drawing responds to the reader. It is laid out the first time its tab opens, and fitted to the width of the page until the reader moves it.

states.description: Its tab has not been opened, so it has no width to be laid out in.
Fitted to the width, at between 55% and 100%, as tall as it needs up to a screen and a half; the zoom out, zoom in and fit buttons sit in its top right corner, and the legend under it.
The part or line under the pointer and its neighbours are lit, everything else fades to a fifth, and a dark tooltip names it and says what a click will do.
A part is pinned: its outline is thicker, its neighbours stay lit, it is moved into view if it was outside, and the inspector at the right holds what the view says about it.
The drawing follows a drag of five pixels or more; the pointer is a closed hand and tooltips are hidden.
A part with a round badge grows from where it is to fill the content area, and after about a quarter of a second the folder it stands for opens. With reduced motion the folder opens at once.

transitions.action: laid out; a state or deployment diagram is laid out both ways and the larger kept

transitions.trigger: the pointer moves over a part or a line, or a part takes the keyboard focus
a click on a part, or Enter or Space on a focused one

a neighbour in the inspector, a row in the tables under the drawing, or another part
the inspector's close button, Escape, a click on the empty drawing, another tab or another folder
a drag on a drawing larger than its frame

transitions.action: the click that ends a drag selects nothing

transitions.trigger: the zoom buttons, the wheel with ⌘ or Ctrl, or a pinch
transitions.action: zoomed between 30% and 250% about the pointer; fit returns it to the width
